projects.name: Rocoto
projects.summary: AI-native ERP for food distributors
projects.description: Rocoto is an AI-native ERP for food distributors. It turns messages and calls into orders, carries them through the warehouse’s night shift, and keeps printed packing sheets, handwritten weights and delivery notes linked to the same records.
projects.status: The released source includes the original order interface, print and paper-readback implementation, provider adapters and persistent backend. The hosted app uses sample records; browser-to-persistent-backend integration, handwriting providers and physical warehouse acceptance have separate verification steps.
features: Resolve customer shorthand against product history, case conversions, substitutions and customer prices.
Print the appropriate A4 or A5 sheet, with layouts for picking, final weights and delivery notes.
Photograph a marked packing sheet. Its QR code identifies the saved print; page registration locates each handwritten cell for review against the original order line.
Import supplier rows, review units and conversions, generate product illustrations, and track stock and lots.
Keep model, parsing, messaging, voice and artwork adapters alongside the business records they support.
projects.audience: Food distributors taking restaurant orders and preparing fresh goods overnight.
projects.problem: Orders arrive in WhatsApp, voice notes, email and calls. Warehouse teams need to identify the right product quickly, prepare it, record its actual weight and get the paperwork out before the delivery run.
decisions: Paper keeps the warehouse’s existing preparation workflow. A saved print manifest gives every cell an address, so readback can match a weight to its exact line.
The order stays the main business object across conversations, preparation, stock and documents.
The design grew through two months with warehouse design partners, with speed during the night shift as the central constraint.

projects.name: Harness
projects.summary: A Codex-based agent harness with generative UI
projects.description: Harness is a Codex-based, vertical-adaptable agent harness with generative UI. A business supplies its domain, tools and interfaces; the harness supplies conversations, files, jobs, approvals, spending records and an SDK for agent-built displays.
projects.status: The source includes the original vertical-adaptable harness and SDK. The hosted bare workspace is a read-only visitor example with an authored display fixture. Managed agent execution needs the operator’s own OpenAI project, allowance and reachable MCP service.
features: Declare roles, tools, recipes, data classes and optional displays for a business.
Use the display SDK to render domain-specific views from an agent’s work.
Keep conversations, scoped files and jobs with the workspace.
Connect approvals, identity and spend accounting to agent actions.
The current source includes managed OpenAI execution; the project retains its Codex-based lineage and architecture.
projects.audience: Developers building an agent application for a particular industry or business workflow.
projects.problem: A business agent needs a place to work: persistent context, scoped tools, credentials, approvals and interfaces for its results. Rebuilding that framework for every vertical makes the domain work harder to maintain.
decisions: The framework owns shared infrastructure; the vertical owns business meaning.
Tools and displays have declared contracts, so a new industry can build on the same harness.
flow: Give a role tools and recipes

projects.name: Manufacturer Order Desk
projects.summary: An AI-native order desk for construction materials manufacturers working across web and email
projects.description: Manufacturer Order Desk is an AI-native order desk for construction materials manufacturers working across web and email. Customers configure products and request quotes online; the sales team keeps incoming orders, product options and email requests in the same workflow.
projects.status: The native app runs the original services with an authored six-article catalogue and sample requests. Client-owned catalogues, photographs and account data retain their original custody. Connected models and providers use your own setup.
features: Review requests with customer, pricing, products and source context.
Edit articles and prices through versioned configuration.
Choose parts and submit specifications through the saved renderer.
Retain quoted values and inspect or restore configuration history.
Use the original vertical SDK and harness integration for the manufacturer domain.
projects.audience: Manufacturers handling product specifications, quotations and customer orders.
projects.problem: A customer request needs to become a clear product specification and quote, while catalogues and prices keep changing. Sales needs to keep the original request, chosen parts and quoted values together.
decisions: Saved quotes keep their quoted values as the catalogue evolves.
The public configurator and internal desk use the same saved configuration and order store.

projects.name: Video Intelligence
projects.summary: CCTV feeds with Cosmos-powered alerts for real-time business intelligence
projects.description: Video Intelligence connects CCTV feeds to NVIDIA Cosmos for automatic alerts and real-time business intelligence. A dashboard brings events and business metrics together; each event links to the source footage for review on desktop or mobile.
projects.status: The read-only native preview opens a retained retail trial with 45 recordings and source-linked footage. Its latest trial has 17 raw observations, all quarantined, and zero reviewed observations. The 68 publisher reference events and generated business history are separate from model observations. Fresh Cosmos processing, real cameras and POS integration need owned infrastructure and acceptance.
features: The original ingestion and processing pipeline connects camera recordings to NVIDIA Cosmos observations.
The designed product brings operational events, alert rules and business metrics together.
Open the source footage behind an event and inspect its frames.
Nine deterministic trackers compute results from admitted observations.
The original harness exposes scoped camera, evidence and tracker tools.
projects.audience: Businesses and developers connecting security cameras to operational alerts and business intelligence.
projects.problem: Security cameras capture the business all day. Operators need relevant events, timely alerts and useful metrics linked to the footage that explains them.
decisions: A model observation keeps its source identity and frame location.
Evidence admission and deterministic tracker calculations are separate from model generation.

projects.name: Rocoto Peru
projects.summary: Mobile AI-native ERP matching bodegas’ Yape/Plin payments to WhatsApp orders
projects.description: Rocoto Peru is a mobile AI-native ERP matching bodegas’ Yape/Plin payments to WhatsApp orders. It brings sales, collections and supplier purchases together, with a working-capital design based on the shop’s trading history.
projects.status: The original mobile interface, encrypted collections service, bank-connection adapters and credit exploration are in the source. The hosted shop uses sample trades and an unconnected bank state. A lender agreement, validated underwriting and funded operation remain to be commissioned.
features: Review orders from existing conversations, with customers, products and preparation together.
Review collections, customer fiado and supplier purchases in the same shop workspace.
Keep payment requests, partial receipts and remaining balances attached to their order identity.
Explore paying a supplier now and repaying later, with the amount, date and terms shown together.
The source includes the Android setup and official WhatsApp connection and history workflows.
projects.audience: Bodega owners who trade through WhatsApp and collect through Yape or Plin.
projects.problem: The order is in a chat, the payment is in a wallet and the next stock purchase needs cash. A shop owner needs a clear view of the money tied to each trade and the obligations coming next.
decisions: The shop’s existing chats are the starting point. Merchant confirmation turns uncertain history into records the owner can rely on.
Customer fiado and the shop’s working-capital credit are different obligations and have different language.
Credit indicators and offer exploration are presented alongside their lender and underwriting requirements.

projects.name: DisDat.dev
projects.summary: A Chrome extension for recording feedback for coding agents
projects.description: DisDat is a Chrome extension that records spoken feedback with the page behind it for coding agents. Talk over what you see in a tab; DisDat captures the elements, styles and page state, then uses a local LLM to turn your words into a precise request your agent can act on.
projects.status: The downloadable Chrome extension is a source beta. A complete recording, local transcription, target capture and rewritten task were verified in Chrome on one Mac. Local mode needs WebGPU, model downloads and disk space; initial downloads take longer than a warm recording.
features: Speak and point while the extension records the page you are using.
Retain selectors, DOM, computed styles, framework state and runtime events with the recording.
Whisper transcribes your speech; Qwen rewrites the request locally while observed page facts remain separate.
Save the structured capture and let the included agent tools unpack it.
projects.audience: Designers and developers giving a coding agent feedback on a website.
projects.problem: A spoken comment such as ‘make this button easier to see’ loses its target when it reaches a coding agent. Screenshots show the pixels; the agent also needs the element, its styles and what the page was doing.
decisions: Requested changes and observed styles are separate. The small local model rewrites the request; deterministic capture preserves the facts.
The default extension runs transcription and briefing locally after downloading its models. Optional provider connections have their own configuration.
flow: Give the capture to your agent

projects.name: Cancha
projects.summary: An Android TV app to watch free Latin American TV
projects.description: Cancha is an Android TV app to watch free Latin American TV. Built for the 2026 World Cup, it combines a channel guide, HLS mirror selection and a rolling buffer for playback and rewind, with a companion web player.
projects.status: The Android TV source builds and has been exercised in an emulator. The hosted web companion uses authored HLS test signals. Channel metadata, feed availability and viewing rights belong to each installation.
features: Browse channels through the original native television interface.
Probe mirrors and select a healthy feed.
Play the current feed and its rolling DVR buffer.
Use the same channel service from a browser.
projects.audience: Latin American viewers using an Android TV and a personal guide of internet channels.
projects.problem: Internet channels have different streams and mirrors. Watching them on a television needs a usable channel guide, healthy feed selection and playback that can recover or rewind.
decisions: The TV app and browser companion share the channel and playback backend.
A bounded buffer makes the rewind window explicit.

projects.name: Leo.casa
projects.summary: Renovation quotes, project chat and milestone payments
projects.description: Leo.casa is a renovation marketplace for homeowners and contractors. They agree on an editable quote, keep the conversation with the project, and review completed work before releasing each milestone through Stripe Connect.
projects.status: The native preview runs the original React and FastAPI app with a private visitor workspace. Quote edits, messages, proof and reviews persist. Real payment and provider operations are commissioned with your own accounts.
features: Edit phases, work, materials and totals in the offer itself.
Discuss the quote and keep messages with the project.
Review changes to the agreed work and price.
Submit proof, review the phase and record acceptance.
The source includes checkout, connected accounts, transfers, refunds, disputes and event handling.
projects.audience: Homeowners planning a renovation and contractors quoting and delivering it.
projects.problem: The quote, conversation, evidence of work and payments often live in different places. Both sides need a shared understanding of what was agreed, what changed and what is ready to pay.
decisions: The quote acts as a shared canvas inside the conversation, so scope and discussion remain connected.
Payments follow reviewed milestones, with financial events and variations modeled explicitly.

projects.name: Farm-to-restaurant route planner
projects.summary: VROOM-based routing for farm-to-table deliveries
projects.description: The farm-to-restaurant route planner is a VROOM-based app for decentralised farm-to-table logistics. Combine shop orders, compare farm sourcing, and calculate pickups, deliveries, capacity and costs on Barcelona’s roads.
projects.status: The native hosted app calculates routes with the same planner, VROOM service and local Barcelona OSRM network supplied by the source. Its nine example baskets use fictional farm names, customers, prices and stock. A new region needs its own road data.
features: Explore the original small-order, larger-basket, clustered-stop and dispersed-stop scenarios, or build your own.
Compare the products and quantities available across farms.
Use VROOM and a regional OSRM network to calculate Barcelona street routes.
Read goods, van, driver, distance and time together.
Edit quantities and calculate above the map, with touch-sized controls and visible capacity feedback.
projects.audience: A logistics service coordinating small farms and independent food shops or restaurants.
projects.problem: Twenty farms around Barcelona said they could not deliver below their minimum order quantities. Twenty shops said they could not afford those quantities. Pooling orders creates a routing and sourcing problem: which farms, which stops and what delivery cost?
decisions: Presets keep basket size and stop density visible as separate assumptions.
Routing and cost assumptions stay editable, so the logistics service can test its actual operating model.
flow: Choose a basket or add orders

projects.name: Vitrina Local
projects.summary: Turn recipe Reels & TikToks into shopping baskets from local grocers
projects.description: Vitrina Local is an agentic commerce app that turns recipe Reels and TikToks into shopping baskets from local grocers. Its shopping agent matches ingredients to nearby stock and returns a basket link in Instagram chat. The original app also includes recipe discovery, saved recipes and video-guided cooking.
projects.status: The original Discover, recipe and basket app and the Instagram-to-cart service are preserved. The hosted app uses authored recipes and shop stock. The animated checkout study illustrates Stripe payment and delivery confirmation; a live Stripe and retailer fulfilment connection is a continuation of the project.
features: Browse recipe recommendations and keep saved recipes together.
Follow the original recipe video beside ingredients and instructions.
Match ingredients and pack quantities, grouped by the shops supplying them.
Receive a shared Reel, extract its recipe and return a basket-review link through the companion integration.
The original work includes the Microinvest POS integration contract and a documented read-only shop-lab prototype.
Return a local-shop basket link to the Instagram conversation. The checkout study illustrates a Stripe payment link and confirmation.
projects.audience: People cooking from online recipes and independent neighbourhood shops listing their stock.
projects.problem: Recipe inspiration is easy to find; a small shop’s available inventory is harder to discover. Vitrina connects the meal someone wants to cook with the independent shops around them.
decisions: The consumer app is built above the independent Social Recipes extraction and player modules.
Ingredients retain their recipe grouping while the basket groups products by shop.
The product connects online recipe discovery to physical shop availability.
The visual checkout study shows Instagram, a Stripe-style payment page and an order confirmation; the connected original release documents basket review and click-and-collect.
flow: Share a recipe Reel in Instagram
Match ingredients to nearby shop stock
Return the basket link in chat
Review and check out the basket

projects.name: Social Recipes
projects.summary: An Instagram agent runtime that turns Reels into recipes
projects.description: Social Recipes is an Instagram agent runtime that turns shared Reels into recipes. It resolves the underlying video, extracts ingredients and instructions, and replies with the recipe in chat. The reusable source preserves its webhook, CDN resolver, extractor and timed video player.
projects.status: The published kit preserves the Instagram webhook and reply helpers, CDN resolver, recipe extractor and timed player. Running the Instagram flow uses an operator-owned Meta app and vision provider. The preview illustrates the conversation; the separate original agent runtime is being reconciled with the published components.
features: Receive shared Reels through the Instagram webhook, resolve their media and return a structured recipe in chat.
Use the original extraction and Instagram CDN-resolution paths to recover usable media.
Turn video and frames into structured recipe information through the configured vision provider.
Share the recipe contract between extraction and downstream apps.
Embed the reusable React recipe-video player.
projects.audience: People collecting cooking recipes through Instagram, and developers building recipe agents.
projects.problem: Cooking Reels keep ingredients and instructions inside a video. A chat agent makes that information usable as a structured recipe while keeping the source video connected.
decisions: Extraction is a reusable layer. Discovery, local inventory, baskets and Instagram commerce live in downstream applications.
The player keeps the source video with the structured recipe.
flow: Receive and resolve the shared video
Extract ingredients and steps with a vision model

projects.name: Hermes Caller
projects.summary: A Twilio dialler with diarised transcripts and Hermes debriefs
projects.description: Hermes Caller is a Twilio dialler with diarised call transcription and Hermes debriefs. The Android app records customer-discovery calls, Deepgram Nova-3 produces multilingual transcripts, and Hermes turns the conversation into a debrief.
projects.status: The Android app, Python server, transcription command and generic discovery-call coach skill are published. The downloadable Android preview starts with empty server configuration. Calling uses an owned Twilio server, and transcription uses Deepgram; the original private Hermes debrief connects through the transcript handoff.
features: Use Twilio’s Voice SDK with a short-lived token from your own server.
Configure the app’s HTTPS server and access key on the device.
Retain each call’s two channels when recording is enabled.
Run the opt-in Nova-3 multilingual and speaker parsing workflow.
Pass the diarised transcript to Hermes for a customer-discovery debrief. The portable source includes a generic discovery-call coach skill.
projects.audience: People making customer-discovery calls through their own Twilio account.
projects.problem: Calling, recording and turning conversations into useful discovery notes involves several tools. A dedicated dialer can keep the call and its recording connected to a controlled transcription workflow.
decisions: The Android app requests short-lived call tokens; provider credentials stay on the server.
Recording and transcription are explicit operational choices with their own configuration.
The call app and the Hermes debrief are separate stages connected by the transcript file.

projects.name: Leo Estimate
projects.summary: Room-by-room renovation estimates from a property listing
projects.description: Leo Estimate is a renovation estimator for Spanish properties. It turns a listing into a room-by-room scope, a priced bill of quantities and before-and-after images, with a printable report for the next conversation.
projects.status: The native preview includes three authored properties and complete cached reports, with 24 calculated items per property. It uses the original interface and recovered project images. Fresh property intake, analysis, image generation and current local prices need their own data and configured providers.
features: Keep listing details, photographs, rooms and comparables together.
Use the original image comparison to explore a proposed renovation.
Inspect room-level work, measurements, materials, labour and price evidence.
Carry the itemized scope and totals into a report.
Continue with the original FastAPI services, durable workers and deterministic costing modules.
projects.audience: Property buyers and investors assessing a renovation, and the contractors helping them.
projects.problem: A property listing shows what is there. A buyer also needs to understand the work, quantities and likely cost before deciding what to buy or asking for contractor quotes.
decisions: The report keeps the visual proposal and its priced work in one context.
Deterministic costing makes the estimate’s arithmetic traceable to quantities and rates.

projects.name: Home Matching
projects.summary: AI-native property scanner across platforms based on the person's lifestyle
projects.description: Home Matching is an AI-native property scanner across platforms, based on a person’s lifestyle. It turns a household’s routines, budget and priorities into a home search, then helps compare listings, save candidates and prepare viewings.
projects.status: The native app opens eight authored homes and deterministically ranks them against household priorities. Favourites, notes and preference changes use a private visitor workspace. Fresh property feeds, mapping, commute and voice providers need their own setup and household validation.
features: Capture required conditions, preferences and their relative importance.
Apply dealbreakers before weighted matching and show the fit and concerns.
Inspect rooms, location and the evidence behind a recommendation.
Save favourites and keep viewing notes.
The source retains the original conversational, map and ingestion workflows.
projects.audience: People choosing a home in Spain and the agents helping them.
projects.problem: Two households can look at the same property and need different things. A useful search needs to explain how each home fits the people moving into it.
decisions: A property’s analysis can be reused. Changing preferences reranks that evidence through deterministic scoring.
Required conditions are checked before softer preferences, so a high score cannot quietly erase a dealbreaker.

projects.name: Retail Location Similarity
projects.summary: Find retail locations similar to your best-performing stores
projects.description: Retail Location Similarity is a geospatial tool for finding locations that resemble your best-performing stores. It converts map data into H3 feature vectors, compares a reference location with candidate areas and ranks the matches on a map.
projects.status: The reusable scorer runs from a fresh clone. Its hosted example computes matches from 90 generated H3 records across five features. The original London matrix contains 131,596 cells and 1,956 numeric features; a full comparison was verified privately. That historical data remains separate while its original attribution is reconciled. Global matrix-building code is preserved.
features: The verified private 54 MB matrix contains 131,596 H3 resolution-10 locations and 1,956 numeric features. Retained builders use Overture Maps Places, Base, Buildings and Transportation; exact per-record provenance is not retained.
Normalize feature dimensions and compute Leo’s historical distance calibration and logistic similarity score; independently expressed functions matched the original on ten real full-dimensional rows.
Exclude the reference cell’s 15-ring neighbourhood and display ranked H3 matches.
A standalone companion runs the scorer on generated sample features; values are illustrative and not observations of London.
Global build scripts and estimates are retained; a completed global matrix has not been verified.
projects.audience: Retail operators and analysts comparing potential locations with a known area.
projects.problem: An operator needs to find places with similar built environment, amenity and access characteristics instead of judging candidates from location names alone.
decisions: Use H3 cells as a common spatial index for location features.
Preserve the independently expressed historical Leo formula and identify its difference from the published DIEM reference implementation.
Bound the private adapter to one fresh calculation at a time and cache three computed examples.
Keep software licensing and the Overture/OSM-derived data rights as separate review subjects.
The operator chooses reference stores using their own performance records; the engine compares their geographic context.
flow: Select a reference London location or enter coordinates
Find its H3 cell and feature vector
Score other cells and exclude the immediate neighbourhood
Review ranked matching cells on the map

projects.name: Geospatial Agent
projects.summary: An AI agent for querying and exploring maps through chat
projects.description: Geospatial Agent is a chat-based workspace for querying geographic data and building interactive map layers. It combines agent tools, Overture data, H3 grids and a deck.gl canvas for examining places, buildings, roads and land use.
projects.status: The recovered Next.js and deck.gl console builds with TypeScript and lint checks passing. Its hosted example shows a computed synthetic retail comparison through the original map renderer. Connect your own model, data and provider accounts to run fresh agent work.
features: Source includes chat, process steps, plan and thought panels driven by streamed backend events.
Next.js, deck.gl and Mapbox components display and control geographic layers.
Backend source includes Overture, demographics, agriculture, climate, routes, news and other tool adapters; each requires its own data and runtime validation.
The source provides a location-selection mode that sends an H3 similarity query and renders returned layers.
projects.audience: Analysts exploring where to locate a business or understand the physical context of a place.
projects.problem: Geospatial questions span many datasets, sources and scales, making it hard to connect an analytical question to inspectable map evidence.
decisions: Keep the conversation, plan and map layers in one workspace.
Stream tool and map events to the frontend as the analysis progresses.
Use separate cascade chat and location-similarity modes in the recovered interface.
flow: Inspect the proposed plan and streamed progress
Select a location for a separate similarity search

projects.name: Leo Vibe Maps
projects.summary: An Airbnb map extension that highlights neighbourhoods by vibe
projects.description: Leo Vibe Maps is a Chrome extension that highlights neighbourhoods by vibe on accommodation search maps. Open a map, show the five original Barcelona areas and inspect their labels. Custom areas use your own Gemini key.
projects.status: The source beta loads as an unpacked Chrome extension. On a live Airbnb Barcelona search, the original integration created all five neighbourhood circles and zoomed to fit. The web example exposes the same five areas. Custom-area requests use a visitor’s own Gemini key for that request.
features: Draw neighbourhood circles on the supported page map; hover and click reveal area information and zoom.
Use the source’s fixed Gothic Quarter, El Born, Gràcia, Barceloneta and Eixample areas.
The popup and background service worker include a Gemini-backed path from a trip description to structured areas.
Manifest V3 content scripts and site-specific handling target Airbnb, Booking.com and Google Maps routes; current compatibility needs verification.
projects.audience: Travellers choosing where to stay while comparing listings on accommodation maps.
projects.problem: A listing map shows prices and addresses while the character of nearby neighbourhoods requires separate research.
decisions: Draw native map circles rather than a static image, keeping areas aligned with map navigation.
Separate the page content script, injected map code, toolbar popup and provider-calling background worker.
Keep the historical browser extension distinct from the separate geospatial agent console and retail similarity preview.
flow: Inspect coloured neighbourhood circles and tags
Optionally provide a trip description for custom areas

projects.name: Artisan Glove
projects.description: Artisan Glove is a sensing-glove design for recording hand contact, vibration and video. I designed a glove and cuff to record the physical signals around a hand interaction. The V4 engineering brings together 20 pressure sites, 20 PVDF contact-vibration channels, two IMUs, an ESP32-S3, a cuff camera and SD recording.
projects.status: Dated ESP32-S3 compile, reproducible host checks and native KiCad/STL design. The canonical main board has 20 unconnected items; separate hand-tile manufacturing outputs exist. Physical assembled V4 qualification is pending. Earlier Bela Mini recordings are documented separately.
projects.summary: A sensing-glove design for contact, vibration and video.
projects.audience: Embedded hardware developers, Researchers recording hand interactions
projects.problem: People studying hand work need footage and touch measurements that describe the same interaction.
features: Two IMUs and a cuff camera.
Native KiCad design, firmware and enclosure geometry, with explicit main-board and physical-build status.
decisions: Keep contact sensing on the hand and recording electronics at the cuff.
Retain pressure, vibration, motion and visual context as distinct capture inputs.
Show the compact appearance concept alongside the actual 112 × 104 × 45.5 mm rigid enclosure.
Keep earlier single-contact-microphone Bela experiments distinct from V4 physical qualification.

projects.name: Messier ’57
projects.description: Messier ’57 is an electric drum with an acoustic feel, played through an amp or guitar pedal. I developed a playable electric drum around a mesh head, microphones and physical sound modelling, exploring a wider palette while preserving the touch of head and rim playing. The prototypes were tested by Ayo Salawu and Dru Masters and exhibited at the London Design Festival.
projects.status: Playable physical prototypes and released browser/Pure Data instruments. The browser substitutes manual Head/Rim/Both selection for the original pickup classifier; its bass kick is a demonstration voice. Original CAD, parts and build notes are included.
projects.summary: An electric drum with an acoustic feel.
projects.audience: Drummers, Electronic instrument builders
projects.problem: Drummers want more sonic range while keeping the touch and gestures they have spent years developing.
features: Actual CHAIR/libpd snare, low-tuned modelled kick and shared room reverb.
Ten two-bar kick/head/rim grooves, tempo and independent per-step snare loosening.
Head/Rim/Both excitation, hold-to-loosen latch, one volume and Stop.
Browser and Pd instruments, original Rhino CAD, BOM, specifications and build notes; visualisation files are separately identified.
decisions: The drum keeps a familiar shell, hoop, mesh head and stand.
A physical control changes the snare response during playing.
Prototype iterations explore the relationship between sensing, touch and sound.

projects.name: Panel Speakers
projects.description: Panel Speakers is a handmade four-channel DML system for spatial DJ sets and home listening. I built four French-polished birch panels with beech frames and two exciters per panel. Stem-separated tracks and a custom MainStage patch place musical parts around the room through a Denon multichannel receiver. The system played at Egg London and was later installed in a bedroom.
projects.status: Four handmade speakers, a working stem-routing setup and real club and bedroom installations.
projects.summary: Handmade DML speakers for spatial DJ sets and home listening.
projects.audience: Club audiences, DJs, Home listeners
projects.problem: A club audience can move between musical parts when the sources are distributed around the room.
features: Two exciters vibrate each thin panel. Instrument stems travel through a custom MainStage patch and multichannel receiver to four separate panels.
decisions: Thin birch faces and shallow beech frames combine broad radiation with a compact physical form.
Two integral wooden tabs at one end provide the suspension points.
The same end becomes the feet when the whole panel is inverted.
Original club and bedroom installations document the built result; new domestic images present the intended product context.

projects.name: Selva
projects.description: Selva is an airborne DNA sampling system for biodiversity monitoring on farms. I developed an air sampler with a custom filter cartridge to collect biological particles for laboratory sequencing. The aim was to help farms understand the species around them and measure changes as they adopt regenerative practices.
projects.status: Exhibited early sampler prototype, retained fabrication CAD and field-trial development.
projects.summary: Airborne DNA sampling for farm biodiversity.
projects.audience: Farmers, Restoration teams, Biodiversity researchers
projects.problem: Farmers and restoration teams need repeatable evidence of the life around a site and how it changes over time.
features: Air passes through a filter cartridge. Collected biological particles are sent for laboratory sequencing; the platform concept connects those results to location and land management.
decisions: A replaceable filter cartridge separates field collection from laboratory analysis.
The sampling enclosure and air passage were developed as printable parts for iteration.
Drone and ATV mounting explored wider field coverage.
Earlier bioacoustic monitoring and later airborne DNA sampling are separate stages of the venture.

projects.name: Speaker Orchestra
projects.description: Speaker Orchestra is an exploration of speakers voiced for individual musical instruments. I made two speakers for a flamenco duo, exploring how guitar and claps could occupy their own places in a room. Different radiating forms and materials were built, measured and tested with listeners.
projects.status: Two physical speaker prototypes, acoustic experiments and exhibition listening tests.
projects.summary: Speakers voiced for individual musical instruments.
projects.audience: Musicians, Installation audiences, Speaker designers
projects.problem: A recorded ensemble loses some of the spatial identity of its individual performers when every instrument comes from the same speaker.
features: Different speaker forms and materials change how sound radiates into the room. The prototypes explore a square framed panel and a separate wooden bowl-shaped construction.
decisions: Each instrument prompted its own radiating form.
Listening tests and frequency-response measurements informed the material experiments.
The speaker occupies a performer’s place in the room as part of the arrangement.

projects.name: Sextet
projects.description: Sextet is a kinetic sculpture that turns seven musical parts into movement. I manually interpreted the instruments in Herbie Hancock’s “Chameleon” as motion, then played the movements through seven servos. With the music in headphones, each wooden ticker becomes a visible part of the arrangement.
projects.status: Working seven-servo MDF sculpture with synchronised, pre-recorded movements.
projects.summary: A seven-part kinetic sculpture driven by MIDI.
projects.audience: Exhibition visitors, Music learners, Performers
projects.problem: Listeners can hear a whole arrangement while finding it difficult to follow the rhythmic contribution of each instrument.
features: Recorded automation in Logic Pro travels through a Python MIDI bridge to an Arduino R4 Minima driving seven servos.
decisions: One ticker represents one musical part.
Manually recorded motions preserve a musical interpretation of the performance.
Startup calibration takes each servo to both extremes, then returns the row to its aligned centre.
Laser-cut MDF and etched instrument labels make the prototype easy to build, inspect and read.

projects.name: Spatial Chamber
projects.description: Spatial Chamber is a fifteen-speaker installation for experiencing recorded ballet spatially. I separated the orchestra in Sylvie Guillem’s “Bolero” recording into instrumental parts and placed the sounds around an RCA photography studio. A projected performance and fifteen floor speakers let visitors move among the music or lie down inside it.
projects.status: Installed and experienced by visitors in the RCA photography studio.
projects.summary: Recorded ballet through a fifteen-speaker installation.
projects.audience: Dance audiences, Small performance venues, Installation visitors
projects.problem: A recorded ballet presents the orchestra from a fixed listening position, while a live performance lets an audience attend to different players and sounds.
features: Instrument stems are arranged in Logic Pro, assigned to hardware output groups and played through fifteen physical speakers around a projected recording.
decisions: Floor-level speakers let visitors choose their position among the sources.
The projected dancer remains visible across the installation.
Stem preparation and output routing connect the recorded orchestra to the room layout.

projects.name: Improvisation Coach
projects.description: Improvisation Coach is a Raspberry Pi practice device with a built-in synthesizer. Plug in a MIDI keyboard, switch it on and play within the exercise on its screen. A Raspberry Pi 4 running FluidSynth supplies the sounds; the small wooden enclosure holds the display, keyboard input, power and headphone connections.
projects.status: Working Raspberry Pi and FluidSynth device in a fabricated wooden enclosure.
projects.summary: A Raspberry Pi synthesizer with improvisation exercises.
projects.audience: Musicians practising improvisation
projects.problem: A musician can start practising more readily with a specific creative constraint to respond to.
features: At startup, the device chooses an exercise. MIDI keyboard input drives FluidSynth on a Raspberry Pi 4, with sound available through the headphone output.
decisions: A randomly chosen exercise gives each session a clear starting point.
The synthesizer lives in the same device as the practice prompt.
A slanted display keeps the instruction visible beside the keyboard.
Finger-jointed MDF, engraved ports and laser-cut fabrication keep the prototype serviceable.

projects.name: Klara
projects.description: Klara is a behind-the-head headset that uses time-of-flight sensors and spatial audio to tell you what’s around you. I designed Klara for the OPPO × RCA challenge: an open-ear wearable that gives visually impaired people a sense of nearby objects and their direction. The band wraps behind the head, with compact sensing and audio modules beside the ears.
projects.status: Developed product concept for the OPPO × RCA challenge.
projects.summary: A ToF headset that describes nearby objects with spatial audio.
projects.audience: Visually impaired people
projects.problem: A wearer needs to locate nearby objects while hearing the environment around them.
features: Time-of-flight sensors measure nearby distances. Directional audio cues communicate where the objects are.
decisions: A band behind the head keeps the ears open and puts the sensing modules close to the wearer’s point of view.
Flush sensing apertures give the latest concept a compact, continuous housing.
Spatial audio carries the directional information, leaving the wearer’s attention on the surroundings.

projects.name: Sound to Movement
projects.description: Sound to Movement is a book examining how dancers turn sound into movement. I studied sound qualities, movement theory and dancers’ responses, then brought them together in a designed book. The spreads pair audio waveforms with movement sequences and Laban Efforts, including the contrasting examples “Erratic” and “Crescendo”.
projects.status: Completed 29-page designed book, with original PDF, print cover and editable publication files retained.
projects.summary: A book about how dancers turn sound into movement.
projects.audience: Dancers, Movement practitioners, Sound and interaction designers
projects.problem: Movement practitioners and designers need a way to examine how particular sonic qualities become gestures.
features: The book places sound parameters, waveforms, movement sequences and Laban Efforts alongside one another for comparison.
decisions: A waveform and a sequence of stills make sound and movement readable on the same spread.
“Erratic” and “Crescendo” compare contrasting sound envelopes and physical responses.
The original landscape format gives the movement sequences room to unfold.
